findings.title: Spawned flusher processes never match multiprocessing.Process, so hung workers are not killed before restart
findings.body: Processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` after `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` checks against the default context process and is false for them. Therefore in `_ensure_processes_alive` a process that is stuck/hung is not killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, leaving two flushers on the same Redis shards; they can concurrently call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` and produce duplicate segments or corrupt the buffer state. The same wrong check at line 346 also means `join()` never terminates a live spawned process on timeout. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or the spawn context's process class) or call `kill`/`terminate` unconditionally for processes.

findings.title: New flusher_processes argument inserted before produce_to_pipe breaks positional callers
findings.body: `flusher_processes` was added before the existing `produce_to_pipe` parameter. Existing callers that instantiate `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` with the old positional order (e.g. passing `produce_to_pipe` as the sixth argument) will now pass a callable as `flusher_processes`; `SpanFlusher` will then use it as `max_processes` and fail or misbehave. The default is also `None`, which makes direct construction spawn one flusher per assigned shard instead of the CLI's documented default of 1. Append the new keyword after `produce_to_pipe` (or make it keyword-only) and consider defaulting to 1.

findings.title: join() stops processing the process list when the timeout expires, leaking remaining flusher processes
findings.body: When `timeout` is provided, the loop over `self.processes` breaks as soon as `remaining_time <= 0` is seen for one process. The earlier `self.next_step.join(timeout)` can consume the entire deadline, so the loop may break before calling `terminate` on any spawned flusher or before reaching later processes. A process stuck in `future.result()`, Redis work, or produce can therefore outlive shutdown and keep flushing shards. Iterate over all processes and terminate each after the deadline rather than breaking out.

findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts negative values and disables flushing
findings.body: The option is `type=int` with no lower-bound validation. In `SpanFlusher`, `max_processes=-1` is truthy, so `self.num_processes = min(-1, len(assigned_shards))` is negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty; no flusher process is started. Spans are then written into Redis without any worker flushing them or setting backpressure, eventually filling Redis and stalling segment delivery. Validate `min=1` or clamp/raise in `SpanFlusher`.

findings.title: Multiprocess flusher path is not exercised by tests
findings.body: Both flusher tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which causes `SpanFlusher` to create `threading.Thread` workers instead of the new `spawn` `Process` workers. The production path (`produce_to_pipe=None`) is untested, so issues with spawn pickling and the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` mismatch can pass CI. Add a test that runs `SpanFlusher` without `produce_to_pipe` for more than one process/shards, ideally with a fake Redis buffer and Kafka producer removed/patched.
